programs.title: Imaging Technologists' Intro to 4D Diagnostic Workflows
programs.grade_or_level: Continuing professional development (adult radiography and lab technologists)
outcomes: Describe how 4D volumetric imaging complements standard 2D X-ray review
Practice patient communication while walking through a 4D injury model
Identify safe boundaries between AI assistance and technologist judgment

sessions.activity: Guided walkthrough of the diagnostic kiosk and monitor workstations; technologists role-play patient intake and discuss what the kiosk can and cannot do, logging open questions.
Pairs practice resizing and rotating a 4D injury image beside its 2D X-ray, then explain findings to a partner acting as the patient.
Union members explore the molecule-viewing lab from inside a structure, discussing how molecular imaging roles may evolve and what training is needed.
Debrief with the Office AI Avatar scenario; draft a union position on AI avatar coverage of off-hours office duties.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized session feedback and task-completion timestamps only; no patient images or personal health data are collected or shared.
programs.consent: Participation is voluntary under a signed CPD agreement; learners opt in to anonymized feedback aggregation and can withdraw at any time without workplace consequence.

programs.title: See Inside: X-rays, Molecules, and 4D Bodies
outcomes: Explain how X-ray images are made and how 4D adds time and depth
Connect molecules to medicine through an immersive lab visit
Practice describing medical images in plain scientific language

sessions.activity: Students tour the kiosk and workstations, sketch the setup, and brainstorm what questions a diagnostic machine should ask a patient.
Working in pairs, students walk around a 4D image of an injury, compare it with the 2D X-ray beside it, and record three differences they observe.
Students step 'inside' a simple molecule, build a paper model of what they saw, and discuss how chemists use such views to design medicines.
Students interview the Office AI Avatar with prepared questions and reflect on where AI helps and where human doctors are still needed.

programs.data_shared: Only anonymized drawings, quiz answers, and observation notes aggregated for curriculum improvement; no personal data or health data collected.
programs.consent: Written guardian/parent consent is required before participation, plus verbal assent from each student; schools receive a privacy notice, no individually identifying data is shared, and families may withdraw at any time.

programs.title: Community Diagnostic Access Workshop
programs.grade_or_level: Adult community health advocates and NGO field staff
outcomes: Assess how kiosk-based diagnostics could expand access in underserved areas
Understand privacy risks of AI-assisted medical avatars
Draft a community consultation checklist for deploying diagnostic kiosks

sessions.activity: Field staff simulate a kiosk health screening with a partner, mapping friction points for low-literacy and multilingual users.
Participants experience a doctor-patient 4D walkthrough and discuss how visual explanations improve informed consent in real clinics.
Role-play an after-hours consultation with the Office AI Avatar; record escalation cases where a human must be reached.
Brief visit linking molecular diagnostics to affordable testing; groups note one access barrier per insight.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized friction-point maps and escalation case notes, aggregated into an open community-access findings report.
programs.consent: Facilitated informed-consent briefing at the start; participants opt in to anonymized contribution of notes; no community members' health data is collected.

programs.title: Nonprofit Health Program Design Lab
outcomes: Map metaverse diagnostic zones to nonprofit program goals
Design a pilot evaluation plan for remote diagnostic services
Identify governance boundaries for AI-assisted health tools

sessions.activity: Teams audit the kiosk setup against a service-delivery canvas: who is served, what is diagnosed, who staffs it, what is missing.
Staff experience the 4D/2D comparison workflow and draft outcome indicators a pilot could measure, such as patient understanding or consultation time.
Review the practitioner-office-as-a-service model; define escalation and human-oversight rules for the Office AI Avatar.
Explore the molecule-editing lab and discuss partnerships with research nonprofits, noting capability gaps honestly.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized canvas outputs, draft indicators, and oversight rules, shared as an open toolkit for nonprofit diagnostic pilots.
programs.consent: Organizational memorandum of understanding plus individual opt-in for anonymized toolkit contribution; participants may exclude their organization's details before publication.
